TRAVEL INSURANCE POLICY WORDING
Issued by Northstar Underwriting
In this policy, "the Insurer" means Northstar Underwriting and "the Insured Person" means the person named in the schedule.

§ 1  Definitions
(1) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Insurer, before any excess, limit or sublimit is applied.
(2) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(3) Dental treatment means treatment of the teeth or gums.
(4) Excursions and tickets means pre-booked excursions, tours, and event or theatre tickets.
(5) Family means the Insured Person's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Insured Person.
(6) Hazardous activity means skydiving, motor racing, or trekking or climbing above 4,500 metres.
(7) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(8) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(9) Physiotherapy means treatment of muscles and joints by a physiotherapist.
(10) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(11) Pre-existing condition means any illness or injury for which the Insured Person received treatment or advice in the 3 months before the policy start date.
(12) Premium means the amount the Insured Person must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(13) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(14) Public transport means any scheduled train, bus, coach, ferry or aircraft.
(15) Qualifying delay means a delay to the scheduled departure of more than 8 hours.
(16) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(17) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Insured Person's details, the covers the Insured Person bought and any extensions.
(18) Sports equipment means skis, snowboards, golf clubs, surfboards and bicycles.
(19) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(20) Territory means the countries in which cover applies, as shown in the schedule.
(21) Travelling companion means a person who has booked to travel with the Insured Person on the same trip.
(22) Trip means a journey that starts and ends in the Insured Person's home country during the policy period.
(23) Valuables means laptops, tablets, mobile phones, cameras, watches and jewellery.

§ 2  Limits and excess
(1) Baggage and Personal Belongings: limit $2,000 per incident; excess $50 per claim.
(2) Emergency Medical Expenses: limit $25,000 per incident; excess $250 per claim.
(3) Trip Cancellation: limit $3,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(4) Travel Delay: limit $750 per incident; excess $25 per claim.
(5) The excess is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

§ 3  Rental car excess
(1) If the Insured Person hires a car during the trip, the Insurer will reimburse any excess the Insured Person must pay to the hire company after accidental damage to the car.
(2) This section applies only to cars hired from a licensed rental company under a written agreement.

§ 4  Trip Cancellation
(1) The Insurer will pay non-refundable travel and accommodation costs if the Insured Person must cancel the trip for a reason beyond the Insured Person's control.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 14 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Excursions and tickets under this section is $300 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation caused by a strike or other event that had been publicly announced before the Insured Person bought the policy.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for cancellation because the Insured Person no longer wish to travel.

§ 5  Inflation
(1) The Insurer may adjust limits at renewal in line with a published index of consumer prices.
(2) Any adjustment will be shown in the Insured Person's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

§ 6  Environmental commitment
(1) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(2) The Insured Person may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Insured Person whether any additional cost would apply.

§ 7  Assignment
(1) The Insured Person cannot transfer the Insured Person's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

§ 8  Contracts (Rights of Third Parties)
(1) A person who is not a party to this policy has no right to enforce any of its terms.

§ 9  Premium payment
(1) The Insured Person must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(2) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

§ 10  Exchange of information
(1) To prevent fraud, the Insurer may check the details the Insured Person gives against public records and industry databases.
(2) The Insurer may contact previous insurers to confirm the Insured Person's claims history.

§ 11  Legal expenses abroad
(1) The Insurer will pay legal costs to pursue compensation for the Insured Person's injury or death caused by a third party during the trip.
(2) The Insurer will not pay legal costs unless the Insurer's legal adviser agrees that the claim has a reasonable prospect of success.

§ 12  Records and evidence
(1) The Insured Person should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(2) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(3) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

§ 13  Cancellation
(1) The Insured Person can cancel this policy within 14 days of receiving it and receive a full refund, provided no claim has been made.
(2) After the first 14 days the Insured Person can cancel at any time; the Insurer will refund the premium for the unexpired period less an administration charge of $15.
(3) The Insurer can cancel this policy by giving the Insured Person 30 days' written notice to the last address the Insurer holds.

§ 14  Instalment agreements
(1) If the Insured Person pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(2) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

§ 15  Interpretation
(1) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.
(2) Words in the singular include the plural and the other way round.
(3) Words defined in the definitions section have the same meaning wherever they appear in bold or with an initial capital.

§ 16  Emergency Medical Expenses
(1) The Insurer will pay reasonable and necessary emergency medical costs incurred during the trip.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for Dental treatment under this section is $400 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Physiotherapy under this section is $300 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for treatment of a pre-existing condition.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for injury or illness arising from a hazardous activity. This exclusion does not apply if the Adventure Sports extension is shown in the Insured Person's schedule.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for any claim arising from the Insured Person's being under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

§ 17  Renewal
(1) The Insurer will write to the Insured Person at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(2) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

§ 18  Claims documents
(1) The Insured Person must provide, at the Insured Person's own expense, original receipts, invoices, reports and any other evidence the Insurer reasonably ask for.
(2) The Insurer may ask for a medical certificate, a police report or a repair estimate, depending on the claim.

§ 19  Subrogation
(1) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Insured Person's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(2) The Insurer can take action in the Insured Person's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

§ 20  Complaints
(1) If the Insured Person has a complaint, the Insured Person should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(2) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(3) If the Insured Person remains dissatisfied, the Insured Person may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

§ 21  Baggage and Personal Belongings
(1) The Insurer will pay for the loss of, theft of, or damage to the Insured Person's baggage and personal belongings during the trip.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for Valuables under this section is $500 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Sports equipment under this section is $300 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by confiscation or detention by customs or other officials.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by wear and tear or gradual deterioration.

§ 22  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Insured Person must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Insured Person must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 23  Third-party administrators
(1) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(2) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

§ 24  Optional cover: Travel Delay
(1) The Insurer will pay reasonable costs of meals and accommodation if the Insured Person's outbound departure is delayed.
(2) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Insured Person's schedule.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for any delay that is not a qualifying delay.

§ 25  Interest
(1) The Insurer will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

§ 26  Compensation scheme
(1) The Insurer is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(2) If the Insurer cannot meet the Insurer's obligations, the Insured Person may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

§ 27  Market conditions
(1) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

§ 28  Accessibility
(1) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

§ 29  Arbitration
(1) If the Insurer accepts a claim but disagree with the Insured Person about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(2) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Insurer.

§ 30  Automatic renewal
(1) Unless the Insured Person tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(2) The Insured Person can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

§ 31  Waiver
(1) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

§ 32  Customer support
(1) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(2) Outside these hours the Insured Person can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

§ 33  Notices
(1) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(2) Notices from the Insured Person should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

§ 34  Taxes
(1) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(2) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

§ 35  Changes in circumstances
(1) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(2) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

§ 36  Recovery of costs
(1) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Insured Person to repay the amount.

§ 37  Governing law
(1) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(2) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

§ 38  General exclusions
(1) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.

§ 39  Duty of fair presentation
(1) The Insured Person must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Insured Person's knowledge.
(2) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(3) If the Insured Person gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

§ 40  Electronic documents
(1) The Insurer will send documents by email unless the Insured Person asks for paper copies.
(2) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer if the Insured Person's email address changes.
(3) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

§ 41  Change of address
(1) The Insured Person must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Insured Person changes the Insured Person's address.
(2) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

§ 42  Data protection
(1) The Insurer will use the personal information the Insured Person provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(2) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(3) The Insured Person can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

§ 43  Salvage
(1) When the Insurer replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Insurer's property.
(2) If stolen property is recovered after the Insurer has paid a claim, the Insured Person must tell the Insurer and either return the payment or give the Insurer the property.

§ 44  Communication
(1) The Insurer will communicate with the Insured Person in English.
(2) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

§ 45  Geographical limits
(1) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(2) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

§ 46  Making a claim
(1) The Insured Person must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(2) The Insured Person must notify the Insurer of a claim within 90 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(3) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

§ 47  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 48  Cooperation
(1) The Insured Person must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(2) The Insured Person must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

§ 49  Currency
(1) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(2) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

§ 50  Personal liability
(1) The Insurer will pay damages the Insured Person becomes legally liable to pay for accidental injury to another person or accidental damage to their property during the trip.
(2) This section does not cover liability arising from the use of motor vehicles, boats or aircraft.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay under this section is $5,000,000 for all claims arising from one event.

§ 51  Fraud
(1) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(2) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

§ 52  Emergency assistance
(1) The Insurer's emergency assistance service is available 24 hours a day on the number shown in the schedule.
(2) The Insured Person must contact the assistance service before being admitted to hospital as an in-patient, unless it is an emergency.
(3) The assistance service can arrange payment guarantees, interpreters and transport home.

§ 53  How to read this document
(1) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(2) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(3) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

§ 54  Payment of claims
(1) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Insured Person's name.
(2) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

In this policy, "the Insurer" means Hearthstone Insurance plc and "the Policyholder" means the person named in the schedule.

§ 1  Definitions
(1) Art and antiques means paintings, antiques, rugs and other works of art.
(2) Bicycles means bicycles and electric scooters.
(3) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(4) Contents means household goods and personal possessions that belong to the Policyholder or the Policyholder's family.
(5) Family means the Policyholder's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Policyholder.
(6) Forcible entry means entry to the home that leaves visible damage to doors, windows or locks.
(7) Garden items means garden furniture, plants and outdoor tools.
(8) High-risk items means jewellery, watches, laptops, games consoles and cameras.
(9) Limit means the most the Insurer will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(10) Outbuilding means a shed, garage or greenhouse within the boundaries of the home.
(11) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Policyholder's schedule.
(12) Portable electronics means laptops, tablets and mobile phones.
(13) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.

(1) Theft: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.

(3) Accidental Damage: limit $5,000 per incident; excess $100 per claim.
(4) Flood: limit $20,000 per incident; excess $500 per claim.
(5) Any limit or sublimit is applied to the assessed loss first, and the excess is then deducted from the result.

(1) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by flood water entering the Policyholder's home.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 60 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Garden items under this section is $500 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for flood damage where a flood warning for the Policyholder's area had been issued before the policy started.

§ 4  Optional cover: Accidental Damage
(1) The Insurer will pay for sudden and unexpected accidental damage to the Policyholder's contents inside the home.
(2) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Policyholder's schedule.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Portable electronics under this section is $500 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by pets.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for wear and tear, or damage that happens gradually.

§ 5  Escape of Water
(1) The Insurer will pay for contents damaged by water escaping from a fixed pipe, tank or domestic appliance.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for Art and antiques under this section is $1,000 per incident.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by water leaking gradually over a period of time.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for damage caused by the failure of grout or sealant around baths and showers.

§ 6  Theft
(1) The Insurer will pay for contents stolen from the Policyholder's home.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay for High-risk items under this section is $2,500 per incident.
(3) The most the Insurer will pay for Bicycles under this section is $800 per incident.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for theft while the home is unoccupied.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for theft where there is no sign of forced entry to the home. This exclusion does not apply where the thief gained entry by deception, for example by posing as a utility worker.
(6) The Insurer will not pay for theft from sheds, garages or other outbuildings. This exclusion does not apply if the outbuilding was locked and the theft involved forcible entry.

§ 7  General exclusions
(1) The Insurer will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Insurer from paying.
(2) The Insurer will not pay for loss of value or loss of use that does not involve physical loss or damage.
(3) The Insurer will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(4) The Insurer will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(5) The Insurer will not pay for any deliberate or criminal act by the Policyholder.

§ 8  Making a claim
(1) The Policyholder must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.
(2) The Policyholder must notify the Insurer of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Insurer will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(3) The Insurer may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.

§ 9  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Policyholder must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Policyholder must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 10  Complaints
(1) If the Policyholder has a complaint, the Policyholder should first contact the Insurer's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(2) The Insurer will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(3) If the Policyholder remains dissatisfied, the Policyholder may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

§ 11  Tenant's improvements
(1) If the Policyholder rents the home, the Insurer will pay for damage to fixtures and fittings that the Policyholder installed and are responsible for.
(2) This cover applies only to improvements the Policyholder paid for, not to items provided by the landlord.

§ 12  Automatic renewal
(1) Unless the Policyholder tells the Insurer otherwise, this policy will renew automatically at the end of the policy period using the payment details the Insurer holds.
(2) The Policyholder can switch off automatic renewal at any time by contacting the Insurer's helpline.

§ 13  Payment of claims
(1) The Insurer will pay claims by bank transfer to an account in the Policyholder's name.
(2) The Insurer aims to pay accepted claims within 5 working days of receiving all the documents the Insurer needs.

§ 14  Customer support
(1) The Insurer's helpline is open from 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. on weekdays and from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on Saturdays.
(2) Outside these hours the Policyholder can leave a message and the Insurer will call back on the next working day.

§ 15  Environmental commitment
(1) Where practical, the Insurer will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(2) The Policyholder may ask for a new part instead, and the Insurer will tell the Policyholder whether any additional cost would apply.

§ 16  Communication
(1) The Insurer will communicate with the Policyholder in English.
(2) The Insurer may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

§ 17  Assignment
(1) The Policyholder cannot transfer the Policyholder's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Insurer's written consent.

§ 18  Premium payment
(1) The Policyholder must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(2) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Insurer may cancel the policy after giving notice.

§ 19  Taxes
(1) The premium includes any insurance premium tax at the current rate.
(2) If the tax rate changes, the Insurer may adjust the premium from the date of the change.

§ 20  Severability
(1) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

§ 21  Third-party administrators
(1) The Insurer may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Insurer's behalf.
(2) Any company the Insurer appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

§ 22  Discounts
(1) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(2) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Insurer may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

§ 23  Alternative accommodation
(1) If the Policyholder's home cannot be lived in after damage covered by this policy, the Insurer will pay the reasonable cost of comparable temporary accommodation.
(2) The Insurer will also pay for the temporary housing of pets that live with the Policyholder.
(3) Cover ends when the home is fit to live in again or after twelve months, whichever is sooner.

§ 24  Governing law
(1) This policy is governed by the law of the jurisdiction in which it was issued, unless both parties agree otherwise in writing.
(2) Any dispute will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of that jurisdiction.

§ 25  Freezer contents
(1) The Insurer will pay for food in a domestic freezer that spoils because of a rise or fall in temperature.
(2) The Insurer will not pay if the freezer is more than fifteen years old, or if the electricity supplier cut the supply deliberately.

§ 26  Waiver
(1) If the Insurer does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Insurer has given up the right to enforce it later.

§ 27  Cooperation
(1) The Policyholder must give the Insurer all the help and information the Insurer reasonably need to settle a claim.
(2) The Policyholder must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Insurer's written permission.

§ 28  How to read this document
(1) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.
(2) Where the schedule and this document conflict, the schedule applies.
(3) Examples given in this document are for illustration only and do not limit the meaning of any term.

§ 29  Subrogation
(1) The Insurer will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Policyholder's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(2) The Insurer can take action in the Policyholder's name to recover any payment the Insurer makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

§ 30  Renewal
(1) The Insurer will write to the Policyholder at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(2) The Insurer is not obliged to offer renewal.

§ 31  Geographical limits
(1) Cover applies only within the territory shown in the schedule.
(2) Cover for property temporarily away from its usual place applies only within the same country.

§ 32  Instalment agreements
(1) If the Policyholder pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(2) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.

§ 33  Changes in circumstances
(1) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(2) The Insurer may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

§ 34  Data protection
(1) The Insurer will use the personal information the Policyholder provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(2) The Insurer will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(3) The Policyholder can ask for a copy of the personal information the Insurer holds by writing to the Insurer's data protection officer.

§ 35  Market conditions
(1) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Insurer will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

§ 36  Currency
(1) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(2) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

§ 37  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 38  Duty of fair presentation
(1) The Policyholder must answer all questions the Insurer asks honestly and to the best of the Policyholder's knowledge.
(2) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Insurer may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(3) If the Policyholder gives incorrect information carelessly, the Insurer may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

§ 39  Change of address
(1) The Policyholder must tell the Insurer within 30 days if the Policyholder changes the Policyholder's address.
(2) The Insurer may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

§ 40  Locks and keys
(1) If the keys to the Policyholder's home are lost or stolen, the Insurer will pay the cost of replacing the locks to the outside doors.
(2) The most the Insurer will pay under this clause is $300 for any one claim.

§ 41  Records and evidence
(1) The Policyholder should keep receipts, photographs and valuations for items of significant value.
(2) Where proof of value is missing, the Insurer may base any settlement on the price of a comparable item.
(3) The Insurer may ask for evidence of how and when an item was acquired.

§ 42  Notices
(1) Any notice the Insurer gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Insurer holds.
(2) Notices from the Policyholder should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

§ 43  Sanctions
(1) The Insurer will not provide cover or pay any claim to the extent that doing so would expose the Insurer to any sanction or restriction under applicable trade or economic sanctions laws.

§ 44  Recovery of costs
(1) If the Insurer pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Insurer may ask the Policyholder to repay the amount.

§ 45  Contents temporarily removed
(1) The Policyholder's contents are covered while temporarily removed from the home to another building in the same country, for up to 60 days.
(2) Contents in a student hall of residence are covered only if the student is a member of the Policyholder's family.

§ 46  Fraud
(1) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Insurer will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(2) The Insurer may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

(1) Headings are for convenience only and do not affect the meaning of this policy.

(2) Any adjustment will be shown in the Customer's renewal documents; limits do not change during a policy period.

(2) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 30 days after the policy start date.

(1) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.

(1) The Provider will communicate with the Customer in English.
(2) The Provider may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

(1) This document, the schedule and any endorsements form one contract and should be read together.

(1) The Customer cannot transfer the Customer's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Provider's written consent.

(2) Notices from the Customer should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

(2) Outside these hours the Customer can leave a message and the Provider will call back on the next working day.

(1) If any loss covered by this policy is also covered by another policy, the Provider will pay only the Provider's proportionate share.
(2) The Customer must tell the Provider about any other insurance that covers the same loss when the Customer makes a claim.

§ 32  Electronic documents
(1) The Provider will send documents by email unless the Customer asks for paper copies.
(2) The Customer must tell the Provider if the Customer's email address changes.
(3) Documents sent by email are treated as received on the day they are sent.

§ 33  Duty of fair presentation
(1) The Customer must answer all questions the Provider asks honestly and to the best of the Customer's knowledge.
(2) If the Customer gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Provider may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.

§ 35  Recovery of costs
(1) If the Provider pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Provider may ask the Customer to repay the amount.

§ 36  Premium payment
(1) The Customer must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(2) If an instalment is not paid within 21 days of its due date, the Provider may cancel the policy after giving notice.

(1) If a device is found after the Provider has replaced it, the found device becomes the Provider's property and must be sent to the Provider.
(2) The Provider may block devices reported as lost or stolen so that they cannot be used on mobile networks.

§ 38  Severability
(1) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.
